parsed.why: No criminalisation, but state-imposed universal exposures: strip-search by birth sex, birth-sex ward exclusion, and an in-force single-sex-spaces code; documented care-denial death. Institutions enforce the hostile rule, so rule of law does not mitigate.

Same-sex conduct and LGBT advocacy criminalised and enforced; trans people arrested and imprisoned for presentation (2023); police sexual coercion, healthcare denial, impunity; no recognition or anti-discrimination law. Current state targeting, not a dead-letter statute.

Thin record: no criminalisation, a 2018 constitutional equality guarantee, only dated societal stigma. No documented trans targeting, but no documented acceptance, protection or recourse either; unresolved signals resolve modestly above midpoint, not to safety.

No criminalisation; courts rule for trans recognition and third-gender markers exist. But documented street harassment, severe rural violence, conversion therapy and rising political hostility. Working judicial remedy keeps it meaningfully above mid-band.

Same-sex conduct criminal, upheld by the High Court in 2024 (up to 10 years). Documented transphobic assault and a trans teenager charged with fraud before withdrawal; no support infrastructure or non-discrimination law, but less active state enforcement than slot 2.
